name: Huaci – AI Translator & Bilingual Reader
summary: Translate selected text, articles, images and PDFs with AI. Read bilingually using hosted credits or your own API key.
privacyPolicy:
Privacy policy: https://huaci.app/privacy.html

Requested text, images and extracted PDF text are sent to the translation service you select. Hosted requests go through https://app.huaci.app and its configured model providers; bring-your-own-key requests go to your chosen provider. Whole PDF files, saved articles and wording preferences remain on your device. Keys and extension credentials are stored locally and are sent only to their respective service. Huaci does not collect browsing history. The public store extension ID identifies the browser channel. When technical and interaction data sharing is allowed, the extension checks its installed version locally every 24 hours and reports upgrades. Hosted requests can include the translation feature. Our server aggregates existing request records by feature to understand usage and response times. If you turn on the off-by-default “Share feature usage” option and allow technical and interaction data, the extension sends daily per-feature counts for bring-your-own-key translation (date, feature, provider, call and failure counts; no content, URLs, languages or models). Accounts and hosted usage are handled under the full policy linked above. Firefox video/audio capture and browser-local Translator features are not enabled in this edition.
releaseNotes: 2.4.0 adds an encrypted local translation cache for your own API key (ChatGPT, DeepSeek and other OpenAI-compatible models) and DeepL. Text you have already translated is reused instead of being sent to the provider again, which saves your tokens and character quota and shows the result instantly. It works for selected text, page regions, website translation, bilingual reading, PDFs, image recognition and alternative wordings; region and website translation show cached passages first and request only the rest. Changing the language, model, style or wording preferences never reuses old results; "Translate again" skips the cache, and Settings can turn it off or clear it. The cache stays on your device and is never synced or uploaded. Credit-based translation does not use it. Translation style guides also gained examples.
reviewNotes:
Firefox desktop 142+. Regular accounts use an email verification code or Google. The initial guest trial allows translation without a login; shared test networks can have exhausted trial credits. No shared test account is provided. Reviewers may sign in with their own email verification code or Google account.

TEST: Install > guest welcome page. Select text on an ordinary article > right-click Translate to <language>. Right-click an empty part of an article > Read this article bilingually; try layouts, Save and word alternatives. Right-click an image > Translate text in image. Toolbar popup > Translate entire PDF > select a local text PDF. Right-click a page region > add translation button. Enable Translate this website, scroll and turn it off. In Settings, test target/interface languages including Arabic, provider switching and account sign-in/out. No payment is required for trial/certification testing.

AUTH: Same-window tab authorization, state and one-use PKCE code. Firefox's random moz-extension origin is never added to a CORS or redirect wildcard. A fixed HTTPS callback on app.huaci.app is observed by the background and routed to the extension's private callback page. Tokens never appear in URLs.

WARNINGS: innerHTML is used for extension-owned UI templates; model translations and article text are rendered as text, not executable HTML. pdf.js is loaded from a fixed extension-local vendor path. pdf.js 6.3.289 and Readability 0.6.0 are unmodified Mozilla distributions with licenses included. pdf.js is configured with isEvalSupported:false and useWasm:false; unsafe-eval is not enabled. The tabCapture/offscreen code is shared with Chromium builds but Firefox removes those permissions, forces videoEnabled:false and hides the corresponding settings and entries. No remotely hosted executable code.

SOURCE/BUILD: Source is available in the public repository https://github.com/csswork/AiTranslation . Requires Node.js 22+, Python 3 and zip, with no npm dependencies or API keys. From the repository root run npm run package:firefox. The resulting dist/extension/ai-translation-firefox-2.4.0.1.zip has the same decompressed files; ZIP timestamps can differ. Complete 24-language catalogs are included, so building makes no translation API calls. The builder converts only the staged manifest and production marker. Vendor origins: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pdfjs-dist/v/6.3.289 and https://github.com/mozilla/readability .

KNOWN LIMITS: no video capture or browser-local Translator on Firefox; no injection into the protected built-in PDF viewer (use the local file picker). No Firefox Android support is claimed.

2.4.0: Local translation cache for bring-your-own-key and DeepL in the extension's IndexedDB. Test with your own OpenAI, DeepSeek or DeepL key in Settings: translate the same text twice and the second result appears instantly with no provider request. Settings > "Cache translations locally" turns it off, shows the count and clears it.
